title: Step Sequencer Tricks
intro: The Step Sequencer is more than a drum grid. Each row can have its own length, step rate, playback mode and start offset, so rows can drift against each other in ways a fixed grid never will.

tips.t: Give every row a different step rate
tips.d: Rows do not have to share the pattern's step rate. Click a row header to select the row, then in the Step Sequencer inspector click Row and choose a note value from the Step Rate pop-up menu. To change just one step, switch to Step Rate edit mode and drag vertically in that step. Hats at 1/16 and kick at 1/8 each run at their own speed.

tips.t: Use the row's Playback Mode for variation
tips.d: Forward, Backward, Ping-Pong, Pendulum, Wander, Shuffle and Random: set one for the whole pattern, or a different one per row. Set just the hats to Random and their step order becomes completely random and nonlooping while the kick stays put.

tips.d: The Step Sequencer supports up to 64 steps per pattern. Longer patterns mean fewer copies and more room for fills.

tips.t: Use Note Repeat for rolls without drawing them
tips.d: Set a step's repeat value to 4 and it fires four times inside that step. Instant trap hats, no extra steps required.

src.label: Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Gate to shorten hits and Tie to lengthen them
tips.d: Gate sets a step's note length as a percentage of the step, shortening it to less than the step's full duration — short gates on a bass pattern give you staccato stabs. It only ever shortens; to make a note run longer than its step, switch to Tie edit mode and click the right edge of the step to tie it to the following one, which lengthens its duration by the value of the step it is tied to. Both are per-step, not per-pattern.

tips.t: Tie steps together for sustained notes
tips.d: Tie mode joins consecutive steps into one long note, which is how you write bass and lead lines rather than just percussion.

src.label: Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Clear a step to reset all its edit-mode values
tips.d: Over-edited a step? Shift-click it to select it, then choose Functions > Clear Step from the Step Sequencer menu bar. That resets all of the step's edit-mode values to their defaults in one move — for step rate, the default is the row's step rate. You can also clear a whole row or the whole pattern.

tips.t: Use the Step Sequencer on any software instrument
tips.d: It is not a drum tool. Put it on a synth, switch the rows to pitches, and you have a hardware‑style note sequencer.

tips.t: Use Skip and Loop Start/End for live rearranging
tips.d: Skip drops a step from playback: the sequencer moves straight to the next step, which shortens the row by that step's length. Loop Start/End sets where the row cycles.
